rules.name: Measures pre-pass (hook and order)
rules.where: Phonemizer.swift phonemize(): call a new TextNormalizer.measures(_:) right after `Self.foldMicroSign(TextNormalizer.linkLabels(t))` and before `custom.mark`, only when `normalizes` is true. In TextNormalizer.rules, delete the merged fix3/reading rules 'Heights: 5'11"' and the three 'Inches' rules (about lines 496-513); this pass replaces them.
rules.trigger: This is the hook, not a reading rule. The sub-rules run in this order: abbreviated feet and inches, marked feet and inches, hyphenated unit, 'N in.' before an adjective, dimensions, single marks, title count, multiplier, game multiplier.
rules.reads_as: Plain text that keeps its digits and gains words ('6 foot 2', '1280 by 7 20', '3 times faster', '27 inch'). The custom lexicon, TextNormalizer.normalize and the number reader then read the rest as they do today.
rules.risks: It must run before the custom lexicon (its '10x', '1X' and exact 'X' entries), and before the units, range and fraction rules. Running first is not enough on its own: the merged height rule inside normalize still fires on text this pass deliberately leaves alone. Today it reads 'The song runs 3'45"' as 'three foot forty-five', '40°26′46″N' as 'twenty six foot forty six inches N', 'Kane 9' 2-0 up' as 'nine foot two to zero', and '6'0"' as 'six foot zero'. So that rule has to be removed, not just run after this pass. Skip this pass when normalize is false (the reference misaki pipeline).

rules.name: Feet and inches, abbreviated (6 ft 2 in, 6ft 2in, 6ft2, 5ft 10)
rules.reads_as: 'F foot M' ('6 foot 2'), or 'F foot' when M is 0. When 'in.' ends a sentence (the end of the text, or a capital follows), its period stays as the full stop. A preposition 'in' is kept ('5 foot 6 in heels').
rules.risks: '6 ft 2 boards' and '8 ft, 2 of them' are left alone. All-caps 'FT' (the lexicon's Financial Times) and 'Ft.' (Fort) are never matched. 'Cut it 6 ft 2 in long' reads 'six foot two long', which is acceptable. The first version of this rule took any spaced 'in', so 'She's 5 ft 6 in heels' read 'five foot six heels'.

rules.name: Feet and inches with marks (6'2", 5′11″, 6’2”, 6'2)
rules.where: TextNormalizer.measures, after the abbreviated rule. It replaces the merged 'Heights' rule.
rules.reads_as: 'F foot M'. Zero inches is dropped ('6'0"' reads 'six foot'). Decimals are kept ('5'6.5"' becomes '5 foot 6.5').

rules.name: Hyphenated feet or inches before a word (10-ft pole, 12-in. skillet)
rules.trigger: `(?<![\p{L}\d.,])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)-(ft\.?|in\.)(?=\s+[\p{L}\d])`. 'in' counts only with its period, so '2-in-1' is untouched.
rules.reads_as: 'N foot' or 'N inch', always singular, because the hyphen makes it a modifier ('a ten foot pole', 'a 2 inch or 3 inch pipe').
rules.risks: Low risk. Today '10-ft' is read 'ten' followed by letters.

rules.name: 'N in.' before a dimension adjective (30 in. wide)
rules.reads_as: 'N inches', or 'N inch' when N is 1, with the period dropped.
rules.risks: Without the period, or before any other word, 'in' stays a preposition ('It's 6 in the morning', '6 in 10 adults', 'a size 12 in men's shoes').

rules.name: Dimensions N x M (2x4, 1920×1080, 10 x 12 ft, 35 cm x 48 cm, 9" x 13" x 2", 2x4x8)
rules.where: TextNormalizer.measures, after the feet-and-inches rules and before the single-mark rule.
rules.trigger:
An operand, then one or more (separator, operand) pairs.

Operand: a number `\d+(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d+)?`, optionally followed by a length unit. The unit is either a mark (', ’, ′, ", ”, ″, '', ’’) or, after an optional space, one of mm, cm, m, km, in., in, ft., ft, yd, px, µm or μm, with no letter after it. 'pt' is not a unit here: it can mean font points or pints.
- A bare 'in' counts only before the end of the text, one of , ; : ! ? ), a period, or another spaced separator.
- 'in.' always counts.
- A straight " counts only when it isn't closing an open quote (the same test as the single-mark rule).

Separator: x, X or ×, either glued on both sides or with one space on each side.

Boundaries:
- Before the first number there must not be a letter, digit, '.', ',', '_', '@', '#', '/', '-', '–', ', ‘, " or “.
- After the last operand there may be a plural 's'. After that, none of these may follow: a letter; '.' plus a letter or digit (file names); ':' plus a digit; '-' or '–' plus a digit; '^'; a superscript digit.
- When the separator is a glued x or X, the first number must not be '0' (hex such as 0x1F or 0X1F).

Leave the text as it is in any of these cases:
- Weight or volume: a weight or volume unit follows any operand, glued or spaced (g, kg, mg, ml, mL, l, L, oz, lb, lbs, tbsp, tsp).
- Time: a time word follows the last operand, after a space or a hyphen (hour(s), hr(s), minute(s), min(s), second(s), sec(s), day(s), night(s), week(s), month(s), year(s), shift(s), session(s)). Example: '3 x 12 hour shifts'.
- A count: the separator is spaced, there is only one, the first operand is a whole number of 12 or less with no unit, and a plural container word comes within the next three words. Container words: tins, pans, trays, dishes, cans, jars, packs, ramekins, moulds, molds, bottles, bags, pots, boxes, cartons, tubs, tablets, capsules, sachets, pouches. Examples: '2 x 20cm round cake tins', '2 x 4 packs'.
- A score: the separator is spaced, no operand has a unit, and the word right before is won, lost, beat, beats, drew, tied, lead, leads, led, trail, trails, trailed, score, scored, scores, ended, finished or final. Example: 'Brazil won 2 x 1'.
- Algebra: the same line has an x next to an operator ('5x +', 'x =', '+ 2x'). Example: 'Factor 3x2 + 5x + 2'.
rules.risks:
A bare spaced times-table fact with no '=' ('Learn 7 x 8 by heart') reads 'by'. A score written without a score verb ('Flamengo 3 x 2 Vasco') reads 'by'. FIBA's '3x3 basketball' reads 'three by three'. These are accepted as rare.

Counts written with x and a unit ('6 x 400m repeats') read 'by', which is how runners say them.

The guards and the frozen cases cover hex, model names (8x7B, 8x H100), file names, version wildcards, algebra, recipe and pack counts, shifts and scores.

rules.name: Single inch or foot mark after a number (27" monitor, 6′ fence, 8' high, 6-8" of snow)
rules.where: TextNormalizer.measures, after the dimensions rule. It replaces the merged inch rules.
rules.trigger:
A number followed directly by a mark, with no letter or digit right after the mark. The character before the number must not be a letter, a digit, '.', ',', '°', ′, '#', or an opening quote (', ‘, " or “). A '-' or '–' before it is fine, so a range such as '6-8"' works.

Which marks count:
- ″: always.
- A straight ": only when the nearest straight " before it on the same line is not an opening quote. An opening quote is a " at the start of the line, or after whitespace or one of ( [ { : — – - / =, with a non-space after it.
- ”: only when every “ before it on the same line has been closed.
- " and ”: never when the line mentions shutter, exposure, ISO, or 'f/' plus a digit (30" is a shutter speed in seconds).
- ' or ’: only before an optional space and then tall, high, long, wide, deep, thick, square, across, away, apart, below or above. Never when 's' follows. Never when an opening single quote earlier on the line hasn't been closed. An opening single quote is a ' or ‘ after the start of the line, whitespace or '(', with a letter after it; '90s doesn't count, because a digit follows it.
rules.risks:
Straight quotes are the main hazard. The frozen cases cover numbers at the end of a quotation ("Give me 5", "Gate 12", "the answer is 42"), quoted titles before 'long' ('Plan 9' long), decades ('90s, 80's), class years ('05), football minutes and shutter speeds.

An inch mark inside a quotation ('"Add 2" of mulch," she said') is a miss, not a misreading.

An arc-second or a ditto mark written ″ reads as inches. That is rare.

rules.name: Title count (3x champion, 4x Grammy winner)
rules.trigger: A number of one or two digits glued to x or X, with no letter, digit, '.', ',', '_', '@', '#' or '/' before it. Then up to two capitalised words or acronyms (Grammy, Super Bowl, Champions League, NBA). Then one of these words: champion, champions, champ, winner, winners, medalist, medallist, Olympian, All-Star, MVP, finalist, nominee, laureate.
rules.reads_as: 'N time' plus the rest ('3 time champion').
rules.risks: The list of title words is closed, so nothing else changes. '3x player' keeps 'ex'.

rules.name: Multiplier before a comparison or a frequency (3x faster, 10x more, 3x as much, 4X the price, 3x a week, 3x over)
rules.where: TextNormalizer.measures, before the custom lexicon and the range rule.
rules.reads_as: 'N times' plus the rest ('3 times faster', '1.5 times faster', '2-3 times faster', which the range rule then reads as 'two to three times').
rules.risks: Algebra is safe, because a comparison is a word and never an operator. A multiplier before a noun or on its own keeps 'ex' (2x speed, 3x zoom, 3x speedup, 4x MSAA, 8x H100, 2x USB-C, 'Set it to 2x'). 'Revenue grew 3x' and 'I've told you 5x already' keep 'ex'; that is deliberate.

rules.name: Game multiplier before an exclamation mark (Combo x2!)
rules.trigger: A lower-case x plus one or two digits, immediately followed by '!'. It must come either at the start of a line, or after a space that follows a word starting with a capital letter (Combo, COMBO, Coins, Wow).
rules.risks: Elsewhere 'x2' stays 'ex two': variables ('Plot x1 against x2.', 'Now solve for x2!', where the word before is lower-case), lane widths (x16), product names (a capital X is never matched). '×3' already reads 'times three' through Lexicon.symbols.

rules.name: Left as they are
rules.where: No change. Lexicon.symbols, the tech lexicon and the number reader keep these.
rules.reads_as: As today: 'two ex speed', 'one point five ex', 'ten-ex engineer', 'ten times faster', 'times three', 'six foot two'.
rules.risks: Speech and frozen cases guard these, so a broad rule can't change them by accident.

open_questions: Halves in sizes: should '8.5 x 11 paper' and the lumber fact 'A 2x4 is 1.5 x 3.5 inches' read 'eight and a half by eleven' and 'one and a half by three and a half', the way people say them? I recommend yes, but only for a .5 inside a size written with x. '15.6" screen' and '1.5x faster' keep 'point'. Two speech cases depend on this.

Sizes written with marks on both sides: should '12' x 14'' read 'twelve by fourteen feet' (the unit once, at the end) or 'twelve feet by fourteen feet'? I recommend once at the end. It is how people say room and pan sizes, and the merged inch rule already reads '9" x 13"' that way. Written units ('35 cm x 48 cm') are still read where written.
Zero inches: should '6'0"' read 'six foot' (what I expect) or 'six foot zero' (what the merged rule says today)? I recommend 'six foot'.
Heights written with abbreviations: should '6 ft 2 in' read 'six foot two', the same as 6'2"? I recommend yes; it works before a noun too ('the six foot two striker').

When x means 'times': I recommend 'times' only before a comparison from a closed list (faster, more, as much, the price, over at the end) or a frequency (a week, daily, in a row). Before a noun or on its own it stays 'ex' (2x speed, 3x zoom, 1.5x, 10x engineer), which matches your call on '2x speed'.
Should '3x champion' read 'three-time champion'? I recommend yes, limited to a closed list of title words.

Recipe and pack counts ('2 x 400g tins', '2 x 20cm round cake tins', '2 x 4 packs') stay as today ('two ex …') for now. When this is decided, I recommend a silent x ('two four hundred gram tins', 'two twenty centimeter round cake tins'), which is how British cooks read them, rather than 'times'.

Game multipliers: should 'x2' read 'times two' only right before '!' and after a capitalised word ('Combo x2!')? I recommend yes. A receipt line such as 'Latte x2' stays 'ex two', because 'x2' at the end of a sentence is just as often a maths variable.
Screen and ad sizes: should '1280x720' read 'twelve eighty by seven twenty', the way people say resolutions? I recommend yes, but only when every side is 100 or more and the only unit is px.
'24x7' was removed. People say both 'twenty-four seven' and 'twenty-four by seven', so I recommend leaving it as it is.

'3x/week' was removed. A reader says either 'three times a week' or 'three times per week'. The multiplier rule rewrites only the '3x'; the '/week' should read the way the slash-per area decides (today the slash is silent: 'three ex week').
review_notes: The repo moved during the review. HEAD is now b06b926 (fix3/reading merged), and its TextNormalizer.rules include a height rule and three inch rules. Because of that, 25 of the 97 speech cases already pass today in both voices, and their notes now say so. The merged height rule also has false positives this set can't freeze safely: '3'45"' is read 'three foot forty-five', '40°26′46″N' 'twenty six foot forty six inches N', 'Kane 9' 2-0' 'nine foot two to zero', and '6'0"' 'six foot zero'. Replace those merged rules with the measures pass before running --freeze. Otherwise any frozen case that touches them would lock in the bug.
